judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear acceleration remedy with an express subjection to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1(o)'s automatic acceleration on insolvency defaults and with 3.4's termination right; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.3's conditions precedent and 8.5's interim relief from the obligation to extend credit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear termination remedy preserving Liens and Obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.4, 3.6 and 3.7(b), which contemplate Lender-elected termination and the prepayment premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "for amounts and upon terms which Lender considers advisable" is a purely subjective standard, though limited to the post-default period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the power of attorney in 4.5(f), which applies the "Permitted Discretion" standard instead — the two provisions describe the same power differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause ends by providing that amounts incurred "shall be Lender Group Expenses", a term that appears nowhere in the definitions — the defined term is "Lender Expenses".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Lender Expenses are charged to the Loan Account under 2.5(c) and paid first in the 2.3(b) waterfall, the undefined "Lender Group Expenses" cannot be slotted into that machinery without repair; 9.1(o) repeats the same error.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such payments and do such acts as Lender considers necessary or reasonable" is broad, and the license to occupy premises "without charge" is stated without time limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 10's self-help rights and 4.4(d)'s storage-access assignment; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed setoff right with an express waiver of advance notice and a post-hoc notification duty; carefully drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1(h) and with the Cash Management Agreement provisions in 2.6(b), which limit the banks' own setoff rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 9.1(g) and 3.6's cash collateral mechanic for Bank Product Obligations; cumulative rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of physical remedies (ship, reclaim, finish, repair, prepare for sale, advertise) and the IP license are drawn for a goods-based borrower and fit awkwardly with a mortgage fund's collateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Borrower Collateral (c032) does include Inventory and Equipment nominally, and 5.16 shows there is essentially no intellectual property, so the clause has little to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as Lender determines is commercially reasonable" places the Code's objective standard in Lender's own judgment, a familiar point of friction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1's chapeau already subjects all remedies to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirement, which qualifies this self-judging language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific 15-day notice period with exceptions tracking the Code; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12, whose deemed-receipt rules expressly carve out Code enforcement notices.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Labelled "(h)" in the text although it falls at position (l), a lettering error; the substance is one short sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1(j)'s sale right; the mis-lettering runs through the rest of Section 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear, with an express "to the maximum extent permitted by law" qualifier on the no-notice receivership.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.2's cumulative remedies; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Labelled "(m)", duplicating the preceding clause's letter, and consists of a pure catch-all ("all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The catch-all sits after a detailed enumeration and alongside 9.2's cumulative-remedies clause; duplicative but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again refers to amounts becoming "Lender Group Expenses", an undefined term, and "deems necessary" appears twice as a self-judging standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic acceleration on 8.4/8.5 insolvency events contrasts with 9.1(a)'s elective acceleration, and the servicing takeover duplicates 4.3(b) and 9.1(e); the cross-reference to "Section 8.5" is garbled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver and cumulative-remedies language; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 15.2, which says the same thing in different words — duplication rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in its sole discretion and without prior notice" governs a list ending in reserves "as Lender deems necessary", an unbounded self-help power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits reserves against the Borrowing Base at any time, whereas 2.1(b) says Lender "agrees not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing" — a direct tension between the two provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compact waiver list; the trailing words "on which such Borrower may in any way be liable" are ambiguous as to what they modify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the broader waivers in 2.13(e); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carefully conditioned on Lender complying with its Code obligations, then exculpates broadly; the structure is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1's commercial-reasonableness chapeau and 11.3's indemnity carve-out for gross negligence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long indemnity ending with an all-caps clause extending it to the Indemnified Person's own negligence, then a carve-out for gross negligence or wilful misconduct; the tension between those two sentences is the classic indemnity dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.2, 16.11's separate indemnity and the Lender Expenses definition; the survival sentence matches 14.1(b)'s preservation of Section 11.3 rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed notice mechanics; the deemed-receipt rule ("the earlier of the date of actual receipt or three (3) Business Days after the deposit thereof in the mail") is workable but the sentence is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Lender address given here (Dallas, Texas 75244) differs from the address printed on Exhibits B-1, C-1 and L-1 (75254), an internal inconsistency in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unqualified New York choice-of-law clause; standard and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2.13(g)-(h), which waive specific California Code of Civil Procedure defenses, and the Code definition's mandatory-law proviso; those provisions assume California law may govern aspects of the deal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exclusive New York venue with a one-sided option for Lender to sue elsewhere; drafted plainly but distinctly asymmetric.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13(a); the asymmetry is deliberate rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard, clearly expressed jury waiver with a knowing-and-voluntary recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13(a) and (b); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence dispenses with the Eligible Transferee requirement for assignments accompanying a disposition of "all or any substantial portion of the business or loan portfolio" — an undefined quantum that can swallow the restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Eligible Transferee definition (c064) and 14.2, and the reference to "the assigning Lender" imports plural-lender drafting into a single-lender facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to "the rights and obligations of a Lender" and "an assigning Lender" in a facility with one Lender, and asserts that an assignment "shall effect a novation", a legally loaded characterisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preservation of Section 11.3 and 16.8 obligations is consistent with those sections; the plural-lender vocabulary is a carry-over from a syndicated form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed-amendment provision limited "to the extent, but only to the extent, necessary"; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates without Borrower signature, which sits against 15.1's requirement that any amendment be signed by Lender and Administrative Borrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but tightly enumerated participation regime with specific carve-outs (A)-(E); the drafting is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Participants are made Indemnified Persons under 11.3 while being denied direct rights here, a deliberate combination; consistent with the Participant definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, with an express subjection to the confidentiality section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16.8(f), which requires prospective assignees to agree to confidentiality.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) — a pledge to "any Person providing financing or other credit support to Lender or any of its Affiliates" — is far broader than the Federal Reserve carve-out that precedes it, and both override every other provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly trumps 14.1(a)'s Eligible Transferee restriction and 14.2's assignment controls, so the enforcement of such a pledge could bypass the assignment regime entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear, with "absolutely void ab initio" for prohibited Borrower assignments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 14.1; the phrase "except as expressly required pursuant to Section 14.1" acknowledges the notice conditions there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear writing-and-signature requirement with a specific-instance limitation; the carve-out for Bank Product Agreements is express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires Administrative Borrower's signature for any amendment, whereas 14.1(c) deems the Agreement amended on assignment without any signature — a genuine inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver language; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates 9.2's second half almost exactly; redundancy rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 makes the initial extension of credit subject to conditions precedent, but effectiveness of the Agreement itself is separate; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — "Unless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement" — is an unusual and opaque instruction whose effect on the many section-specific provisions is hard to state.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would generalise section-limited rules such as the Affiliate 10% deeming rule (c008) and 1.2's financial-covenant meaning of "Borrower", which are expressly confined to particular sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An express disclaimer of contra proferentem coupled with a recital that "this Agreement has been reviewed by all parties"; whether such a clause can displace the rule is itself contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on how every one-sided provision in the instrument (Lender's sole discretion, Permitted Discretion, satisfaction standards) would be construed, so it is the natural battleground for a Category 1.3 argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says only that provisions are "severable ... for the purpose of determining the legal enforceability of any specific provision" — it never states what happens if a provision is held unenforceable, which is the whole point of a severability clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That gap matters against 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause and 2.13(d)'s "irrespective of the validity ... of this Agreement", which assume some machinery for partial invalidity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully constructed gross-up with a defined "Taxes", a net-income exclusion and a gross-negligence proviso; the internal reference to "the penultimate sentence of this Section 16.5" is imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Taxes" cross-reference in the definitions (c159); the "without setoff, counterclaim, or other defense" opener aligns with 2.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause with an express statement that failure to deliver originals does not affect validity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.4's rule that a Record satisfies writing requirements; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "or elects to do so upon the reasonable advice of its counsel" lets Lender revive Borrower liability by voluntary election, a notably one-sided trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13(i)'s reinstatement provision; the Voidable Transfer definition (c164) cross-refers here correctly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of seven exceptions, each specific; clause (d)'s "as requested or required by any Governmental Authority" is broader than the rest but still bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 14.1(e) and the survival reference in 14.1(b); the two-year survival is a clear term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statutory notice with no operative obligation on either party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Free-standing; nothing elsewhere depends on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause bars contradiction by "any other agreement, oral or written, before the date hereof" — it says nothing about contemporaneous agreements and contains no conventional merger language, leaving its exclusionary reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument repeatedly incorporates extrinsic material (Borrower's Required Procedures, the written description underlying a Permitted Reorganization, the Offering Circular), which sits uncomfortably with an entire-agreement clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines an irrevocable agency appointment (which the same sentence then makes revocable on notice) with a broad indemnity against claims by "any third party whosoever"; the irrevocable/revocable pairing is internally awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indemnity's carve-out refers to "any Lender" and "Lender-Related Person" inconsistently with the operative words, and the appointment interacts with 2.13's joint and several liability and the "Borrower"/"Borrowers" definition (c031).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form with blanks left unfilled and bracketed alternative text still in place, so the notice cannot be read as a completed instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Lender address shown (Dallas, Texas 75254) differs from the notice address in Section 12 (75244), and the recital omits "between" and mis-describes the parties compared with the preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 6 certifies compliance with "Sections 7.16, and 7.37" — there is no Section 7.37, and the stray comma compounds the error; paragraphs 2 and 5 also duplicate each other with different carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is 7.17, which 6.3 identifies as the financial covenant to be certified, so the exhibit is out of step with the operative reporting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form with unfilled blanks and bracketed optional text; otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.12(b)'s LIBOR Deadline and the Interest Period definition, but the address again reads 75254 rather than Section 12's 75244.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names an account holder as "B-4 PARTNER, LLC" rather than B-4 Partners LLC, and the schedule combines a specific account with an open-ended substitution formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Designated Account definition (c059) simply points to this schedule, but the schedule adds a Control Agreement requirement not stated in 2.8; and 2.6(a) requires Wells Fargo to be the sole Cash Management Bank after 60 days while this account is at Greater Bay Bank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account number is redacted or garbled in the executed text, but the substitution formula is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.3(a) and 2.6(b)(iii), which direct payments and sweeps to Lender's Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item 2 refers to "the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt", a capitalised term that is not defined anywhere in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes that Approved Debt will be secured, which cannot be squared with Subordinated Debt (c152)(a)'s "unsecured" requirement, and it depends on the grammatically broken proviso in Permitted Liens (c130)(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual list of two licences; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 represents that this schedule lists "all" required licences for the business as conducted and "proposed to be conducted", which is a strong claim against so short a list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two entries, one of which is a location described only functionally ("at Lender's offices or office of a custodian").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 represents Collateral is located only at scheduled locations while permitting public-warehouse storage of certain loan files; this schedule does not list any warehouse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "SUBSIDIARIES - NONE" is consistent with Schedule 5.8 and with the narrowed Subsidiary definition (c155), even though covenants throughout address Subsidiaries at length.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single address; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the 3.1(o) landlord waiver location and Schedule 5.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The organizational identification numbers are illegible or redacted in the executed text, so the schedule as reproduced states nothing usable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.7(c) represents that these numbers "are identified on Schedule 5.7(c)", so the illegible entry undercuts that representation and 7.5's prohibition on changing them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One word; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.7(d) and 4.4(b)'s after-acquired claim mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and narrative, with a stray comma in "5,871,017,93 Units" and a description of Units and Interests that does not map cleanly onto the defined terms "Stock" and "Investor Membership Interest".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It discloses that members' Interests are redeemed in the Manager's discretion in the ordinary course, which is squarely in tension with 7.10's prohibition on Restricted Payments (including redemptions) and with the Permitted Reorganization machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short narrative disclosure with a typographical slip ("who's mortgage"); its content is factual rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.10 carves out matters disclosed here from the no-litigation representation, and the second paragraph describes a senior lien on property securing a loan — relevant to Eligible Notes Receivable clause (b)'s first-priority requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One word; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms that the elaborate IP covenants in 4.4(c) and the IP license in 9.1(i) have nothing to operate on — surplusage rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Account numbers are partly redacted and the entries are compressed, but the accounts are identifiable by function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lists Greater Bay Bank as holding the Cash Management Account, which 2.6(a) requires to move to Wells Fargo within 60 days, and Schedule 2.6 (Cash Management Banks) is not reproduced at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short items; definite, though item 1 simply cross-refers to Schedule 5.8 rather than giving the detail 5.20 requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(b) permits only Indebtedness "set forth on Schedule 5.20", so the single Fremont Bank loan is the entire permitted stock of existing debt — a tight fit with Permitted Liens item 1 on Schedule P-1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is reproduced as a mangled two-column table in which company names run together ("Land America Title Insurance Company -Ticor Title Insurance Company Co."), so which entities are approved cannot be read with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.21 and the Approved Title Insurance Company definition (c013) make this list operative for eligibility and Settlement Agent purposes, so the garbled entries matter to those provisions.
